name: Motor Scooter
description: A low-speed motorcycle with a step-through frame or a footrest platform, wheels over 16 inches, 2 or more brake horsepower (1,500 W) and a design speed of no more than 50 mph. Its definition is written in engine terms (over 50 cc), but Kentucky counts a plug-in battery-powered one as an electric motorcycle.

restrictions.rule: A step-through frame or a platform for the operator's feet, and wheels more than 16 inches in diameter (Kentucky Revised Statutes §186.010(24))
2 brake horsepower (1,500 W) or more, designed to go no faster than 50 mph (Kentucky Revised Statutes §186.010(24))
Not a moped: Kentucky's moped definition requires a combustion engine of 50 cc or less
Riders need a motorcycle operator's license or motorcycle instruction permit (Kentucky Revised Statutes §189.2851)
Under the motorcycle helmet law: riders and passengers under 21, permit holders and riders licensed less than a year must wear a helmet (Kentucky Revised Statutes §189.2851)
Titled and registered as a motorcycle; a plug-in battery-powered one also pays Kentucky's annual electric motorcycle fee (Kentucky Revised Statutes §189.2851)
Must be insured, with proof of insurance carried while riding (Kentucky Revised Statutes §189.2851)
Must meet the same equipment standards as a motorcycle and follow the rules of the road (Kentucky Revised Statutes §189.2851)
